analysis.title: Power & Infrastructure Weekly Recap & Week Ahead
key_insights: Needham's power and infrastructure coverage fell about 15.6% on average last week (median -16.2%), against XLU +1.9% and GRID -6.1%. Needham says concern moved from AI demand to construction costs and dilutive financing risk.
Data center capex is increasingly underwritten above $13MM/MW excluding GPUs. CIFR's Barber Lake budget rose to about $2.95B (~$14MM/MW) alongside an unexpected $850MM convertible offering.

Project-level financing spreads are widening and developers lean more on institutional project bonds. Leasing visibility is limited ahead of the November elections, and ERCOT Batch Zero determinations are expected in December.

Needham views the sell-off as a repricing of financing and execution risk, not a structural fall in power demand. A sustained recovery needs project financings closing at attractive loan-to-cost ratios, stable construction budgets and higher NOI per MW on new leases.

Last week's leaders were FSLR (-2.9%), ITRI (-3.0%) and NXT (-7.0%). Laggards were EOSE (-27.8%), TE (-22.7%) and FLNC (-21.9%). Data center-exposed names fell sharply: SEI -18%, BW -15%, GNRC -14%, PRIM -12%.
By subsector, Nuclear: Reactors (-19.2%) and DC Power & Cooling (-16.5%) were weakest for the week. Renewable Developers (-4.1%) and IPPs (-5.1%) were strongest. The universe average was -10.9%.

ITRI reports 3Q26 on 10/27 with guidance of $590-600MM revenue and $1.50-1.60 non-GAAP EPS. It has beaten EPS for 15 straight quarters and rallied about 26% after its 2Q26 print. 2Q26 orders of $550MM against a flat ~$4.4B backlog pushed trailing-12-month book-to-bill below 1x. Needham wants 2H26 bookings back above 1x.
ITRI shares trade at about 11x CY27E consensus EBITDA, about 41% below the 52-week high. ARR is $417MM.

NXT and FSLR held up better. Needham gives three reasons: possible policy upside from a stronger Democratic midterm showing, less direct exposure to bespoke data center construction and financing than bring-your-own-power providers, and valuation supported by earnings and cash generation.

NXT reports 2Q FY27 on 10/28 AMC after July's move to the low end of FY27 guidance (revenue $4.1-4.4B, adj. EBITDA $870-930MM, adj. EPS $4.42-4.73). Needham expects FY28 and multi-year targets at the November 16 Capital Markets Day. NXT trades at about 16x Needham's FY28E adj. EPS of $4.97.
FSLR reports 3Q26 on 10/29 AMC. Watch items are bookings, pricing and the outlook against a 45.1 GW contracted backlog. Post-232 contracting is measured against a ~$0.36/W pre-232 clearing level.

TE fell about 23% to $2.62, about 79% below its 52-week high. Investor inbounds focus on financing. A $30MM Evervolt tranche was due 10/15 and $18MM is due 10/30. The July $120MM convert covered about a third of ~$310MM remaining G2 Austin Phase 1 capex.

Section 232 import floors effective 12/4 set a benchmark of about $0.44/W for imported modules including an additional 15% duty. Needham sees this as supporting TE's 2027+ competitive position if financing and execution come together.
SEI, PRIM and NEOV are Needham's top ideas. SEI and PRIM sold off on no company-specific news.

SEI raised guidance on 9/8: 3Q26 adj. EBITDA $110-130MM, 4Q26 $145-180MM, 1Q27 $200-240MM, backed by contracted Stateline and Hatchbo capacity. PT is $104 (from $98), about 8x Needham's FY27E adj. EBITDA of $852MM. 3Q26 results are expected 11/3 AMC.

PRIM trades at about 13x Needham's FY27E adj. EPS of $5.50. Catalysts are mechanical completion of the last problem project in early November, $1.5-2.0B of 2H26 renewables awards, and the 3Q26 print on 11/2. The top-ideas page gives a $165 PT while the mentioned-companies header lists $172.

NEOV fell 16% despite signing its first binding C&I order, a Lion Power MSA with about $10MM minimum commitments through 2027 and more than $4MM of initial POs shipping in 4Q26. Needham calls it modest next to the ~$53MM non-binding IGC reservation. Next milestones are SK On definitive documents, a non-IGC utility-scale PO and the December Line 1 ramp.

BNEF's 2H26 outlook cut the 2026-2036 US utility-scale solar forecast 7.5% to about 430 GW, citing tariffs and faster tax-credit phaseout. It raised the US storage forecast 35% to 383 GW through 2036. Nuclear additions are 13.7 GW through 2036. Gas could add up to 67.8 GW through 2030 against 14.3 GW of retirements.

BNEF's data center capacity forecast is 118 GW by 2030, up 52% from December 2025. Needham calls the revisions constructive for utility-scale BESS and near-term solar execution, more cautious for post-tax-credit solar development, and favorable for gas over new nuclear.

Fermi (NR) secured AMD credit support for a 222 MW Project Matador lease with a framework of up to 650 MW. The phase-one lease is 15 years, about $6.5B of contracted revenue, 156 MW critical IT, with project NOI margins of 75-80% and deliveries from 4Q27. AMD support takes effect only after construction completes and rent starts on the final phase, so it does not solve construction funding.

Baker Hughes, Venture Global and GE Vernova signed a Power Frame Agreement for up to 16 behind-the-meter power islands, with deliveries 2028-2034. The first PO is expected by year-end 2026 and financial terms were not disclosed.
Mainspring signed a 1.6 GW linear generator agreement with AEP through 2034, with a firm initial 190 MW for delivery from 2027.

Oklo's Groves-2 Forge was selected for the DOE Nuclear Energy Launch Pad. Needham says this has limited near-term financial impact. Conversion of the Meta Ohio prepayment into a PPA and the 3Q26 update (est. 11/10) matter more.

NNE's KRONOS construction permit is in NRC review. Final environmental assessment is targeted for May 2027 and final safety evaluation for September 2027, with initial construction in 2H27. This is not a permit approval.

Cardinal Infrastructure (CDNL, NR) agreed to buy Hughes Brothers for $357.5MM plus up to $97.5MM earn-out (~$455MM total). Hughes had over $220MM trailing revenue and ~$350MM backlog, with pro forma net leverage of 1.4x.

Hyperscaler capex for MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META and ORCL is $808bn in CY26E (+96% y/y) and $1,078bn in CY27E (+33%), versus $412bn in CY25A. META (10/21 AMC) and MSFT (10/28 AMC) earnings are AI infrastructure read-throughs.

Coverage valuation: median EV/EBITDA is 12.1x CY26E and 8.4x CY27E. FSLR is 6.3x CY26E and LEU 33.0x. Median short interest is 12.4% of shares outstanding and the median name is 64.2% below its 52-week high.

tension_points.bull_case: Needham sees the sell-off as a repricing of financing and execution risk, not weaker power demand. Contracted capacity such as SEI's Stateline and Hatchbo underpins EBITDA, and BNEF raised its 2030 data center capacity forecast to 118 GW.
tension_points.bear_case: Construction costs above $13MM/MW, an unexpected $850MM CIFR convertible, wider project financing spreads and limited leasing visibility ahead of the midterms point to dilution and execution risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained recovery requires project-level financings closing at attractive loan-to-cost ratios, stable construction budgets and higher NOI per MW on new leases.

tension_points.bull_case: Section 232 import floors from 12/4 set a ~$0.44/W benchmark for imported modules, supporting a stronger 2027+ competitive outlook.
tension_points.bear_case: The G2 Austin Phase 1 package is unresolved, Evervolt tranches ($30MM due 10/15, $18MM due 10/30) may settle in equity, and each leg lower raises the effective cost of equity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to close the debt-led G2 Austin Phase 1 financing without excessive dilution.

tension_points.bull_case: Large IOU RFPs in California and Illinois could return book-to-bill above 1x. The company has beaten EPS for 15 straight quarters.
tension_points.bear_case: 2Q26 orders of $550MM against a flat ~$4.4B backlog pushed trailing-12-month book-to-bill below 1x, and the ~26% post-2Q rally raises the bar.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 2H26 order momentum failing to lift book-to-bill back above 1x at the 3Q26 print on 10/27.
